category.name: Plan the Network and Capital Programme

derivation: STANDARDS-DERIVED. Citation statuses observe source_status_ceiling. Network demand is GFMAM 3.2 and APQC 10.2.2; the capital programme is APQC 10.2.1 and ISO 55001:2024 cl. 6.2.2; whole-life value is GFMAM 3.6 and ISO 55001 cl. 8.1. Gas class, HCA and MAOP are 49 CFR 192.5, 192.609, 192.611, 192.903 and 192.905. Electric jurisdiction is 16 U.S.C. 824o. IEEE 1729 is in model.json derivation and is not in the Source Authority Pack, so it is not cited. 3.1 continues to forecast WORK demand. 2.4.1 validates the item against the programme 17.4 produces.
field_set: EN 17007:2017 cl. 5.2 maintenance process profile, corroborated by ISO 9001:2015 cl. 4.4.1 a) to h).
gaps: IEEE 1729-2025 is named in model.json derivation for this category and is not in the Source Authority Pack. It is not cited. Electric distribution network-planning method is therefore ISO 55001 cl. 6.2.2, GFMAM 3.2/3.4, IEC 61968-6 NE/SIM, and APQC 10.2.2 as structure.

EN 17007 assumes the item already exists. Network planning, capital programming and whole-life value are asset-creation and asset-management-planning, not maintenance. MAN, OPT, IMP, MRQ, DTA and BUD are nearest-process mappings. ISO 55001:2024 cl. 6.2.2 and cl. 8.1 are the real spine. Say so rather than stretching CEN into a planning statute.

No pack source states network-demand forecast arithmetic, power-flow or pressure-drop arithmetic, a portfolio score, NPV or a risk-cost formula. 17.1.1, 17.2.2, 17.4.2 and 17.5.1 are therefore SPEC - a determination whose rule no source states - not DMN and not 'standing'.
NERC TPL and PRC bind the bulk-power system. 16 U.S.C. 824o(a)(1) and (i)(1) keep them off local distribution. 17.2.3 names them only when 17.3.4 returned bulk-power.

49 CFR 192.5(d) record-keeping names gas transmission segments. Class location still classifies locations for the whole part. 192.609/611 class-change study and MAOP confirmation are steel above 40 percent SMYS. 192.611(a)(4)(vii) bars the eligible-Class-3 IM path for gathering and distribution. 17.3.2 returns that bar as a class, it does not invent a distribution MAOP rule.

Subpart O HCA and covered-segment (192.903, 192.905) are transmission. Distribution is DIMP under 192.1001-1015. 17.3.3 returns DIMP-distribution as a class with that authority, so 8.0 does not apply HCA obligations to a main.
IEC 61968-11 Work package has no NetworkDemand, ClassLocation or HCA class. The classification is held as Asset plus WorkActivityRecord.
IEC 61968-6 cl. 4.2 NE is network extension planning and SIM is network operation simulation. There is no capital-programme component; the plan sits on NE and the money on FIN.

APQC 10.2.1 and 10.2.2 close this category structurally (pcf_id 19209, 19213). They are consensus structure, not content. 10.2.3.1 Develop construction strategy (pcf_id 19220) still has no model home - that is a finding for 2.0, not a process to add here.

2.4.1 already validates funding for one work item. 17.4 produces the programme it checks. 3.1 already forecasts work demand. 12.5 still owns maintenance strategy. 12.6.3 still owns replacement and renewal of a single asset. Those boundaries are in the process text.
Real-time monitoring, alarm handling, optimisation and protection settings remain out of scope (APQC 14.1.4 is scope). 17.1.3 tests planning cases; it is not the control room.

merge_corrections.what: ONE CORRECTION. 17.2.2 and 17.5.2 arrived with identical inputs (option set from 17.2.1, whole-life basis from 17.5.1, classification from 17.3) and identical outputs (a comparison, to FIN and to 17.2.6), and with opposite notation - SPEC and BPMN - for what would then be one act. The submission saw the collision and tried to hold it apart in a control, but a published basis applied to an option set is one application, not two. Resolved by giving 17.5.2 the arithmetic it already claimed and re-scoping 17.2.2 to the thing no source prices: weighing that comparison against deliverability, consent and the 192.611(d) and 192.905(c) clocks. 17.2.2 now consumes 17.5.2 rather than duplicating it, and stays SPEC because nothing states how an unpriced constraint is weighed against a priced comparison. Both processes are in model.json, so the overlap is the taxonomy's and not the submitter's - recorded here so the next reader knows which one owns what.
accepted_from_submitter: 17.3.3 returns DIMP-distribution as a class with 49 CFR 192.1001 as its authority, so 8.0 cannot apply Subpart O high-consequence-area obligations to a distribution main. This is the coordination 17.0 was sequenced ahead of 8.0 for, and it arrived without being asked for.

192.611(a)(4)(vii) bars the eligible-Class-3 integrity-management path for gathering and distribution lines, and 17.3.2 returns that bar as a class rather than inventing a distribution MAOP rule. Correct, and the kind of negative finding this reference is built on.

IEEE 1729-2025 is named in model.json's derivation for this category and is not in the Source Authority Pack. The submission refused to cite it and said so. That is the rule working: model.json's derivation line is now the thing to fix, not the specification.

Four SPEC processes, each justified as a determination whose rule no source states - forecast arithmetic, whole-life weighting, portfolio score, cost basis - rather than as 'standing'. This is the second SPEC case used correctly by another platform.
EN 17007 is named as the wrong spine for asset creation and ISO 55001 cl. 6.2.2 and cl. 8.1 named as the right one, instead of stretching CEN into a planning statute.
16 U.S.C. 824o(a)(1) and (i)(1) used to keep NERC TPL and PRC off local distribution, consistent with 7.0's treatment of FAC-003 and with 17.3.4.
merge_corrections.models_built_here: Nine artifacts, 5 BPMN and 4 DMN. Grok specifies them and cannot build them; only this side has the generator.
